forecasts.title: Will Tesla or SpaceX announce a definitive, binding agreement for Tesla to acquire SpaceX, SpaceX to acquire Tesla, or the two entities to merge or combine in any structure that results in a transfer
forecasts.reason: hunt chose NO but its own numbers refuse it: side price 0.96, own edge +2.0pt vs fee 0.3pt — It's the most liquid market on the list and its resolution hinges on a verifiable, high-bar corporate event (a signed definitive merger agreement) whose necessary public precursors — special committee, bankers, S-4/proxy machinery — demonstrably do not yet exist, whereas the other candidates turn on ambigu
forecasts.dossier:
BASE RATE. Kalshi requires a *definitive, binding* agreement announced via official channel before Oct 1 — Musk expressions of intent, negotiation updates and hypotheticals are explicitly excluded. Controller-conflicted megadeals of this scale require dual independent special committees, independent bankers, fairness opinions and an S-4/proxy; historically such processes run 3–6+ months and leak ('in advanced talks', 'committee retains Centerview/Evercore') well before signing. Deals essentially never get signed with zero visible precursors 18 days out. Even conditioning generously on a deal eventually happening (~50%, in line with sell-side), spreading announcement risk over Sep-2026→mid-2027 gives ~3% for an 18-day slice, and the near-term hazard should be *below* average because the precursors are absent.

RESEARCH. As of Sep 12, 2026 there is no formal process. Musk on the Jul 22 Q2 call cited 'more and more overlap' but said combination 'can't be talked about on an earnings call — it's got to be done with the appropriate process.' Motley Fool (Aug 6) states explicitly: no special committee, no investment bankers, no timeline; companies have not confirmed talks. SpaceX IPO'd Jun 12, 2026 (Nasdaq: SPCX, ~$135/sh, ~$1.75T) — a merger 3 months post-IPO would collide with the ~180-day underwriter lock-up expiring ~Dec 9. Tesla's actual September calendar is Cybercab/Semi/Roadster product events, not M&A. No Tesla 8-K or S-4 exists.

CROWD NARRATIVE. Wedbush's Ives puts 80–90% 'by early 2027'; ARK says 'announcement possible before year-end'; Shotwell hinted at a *post-IPO* merger. These are all Q4-2026-to-2027 framings, yet retail collapses 'it's coming' into 'it could be any week,' sustaining a 4–5c Musk-tease premium on an 18-day window. That is the distortion.

OTHER SIDE. YES holders (207k open interest) believe Musk can move unilaterally given ~80% SpaceX voting control and that a surprise 8-K could land at any moment, possibly timed to Tesla's November annual meeting.

FALSIFIER. Any of: a Tesla or SpaceX 8-K disclosing special-committee formation, credible Reuters/Bloomberg/WSJ reporting that either board has retained independent financial advisers for a combination, or an S-4 filing. Any of those before ~Sep 25 would mean I am wrong and the 4c is cheap.

forecasts.title: When will Anthropic officially announce an IPO?
forecasts.reason: The resolution trigger is a mechanically-constrained regulatory sequence (public S-1 → mandatory 15-day gap → roadshow → pricing) whose current state is verifiable on EDGAR and whose schedule was explicitly reported by Reuters six days ago, so primary sources pin the timeline far more tightly than the crowd's 28c.
forecasts.dossier:
RULES FIRST. Kalshi resolves YES only if (1) SEC declares the S-1 effective, (2) the IPO is priced, or (3) an exchange assigns a ticker. A public S-1 naming a proposed symbol does NOT count — an application is not an assignment. Natural experiment confirming this: Oura publicly filed its S-1 on Sep 3, 2026 naming Nasdaq ticker 'OURA', yet Kalshi's KXIPOOURA-26OCT01 trades 0.61, not ~1.00. So YES here requires actual pricing/effectiveness before Oct 17.

STATE OF PLAY. Anthropic confidentially submitted a draft S-1 on June 1, 2026. As of today (Sep 11) EDGAR shows no public S-1 or S-1/A — the prospectus has not flipped. Reuters (via CNBC, Sep 5) reported the public S-1 slipped to late September, the roadshow is 'unlikely to begin before mid-October,' and the listing targets the days just before the Nov 3 midterms. Underwriters: Morgan Stanley, Goldman, JPMorgan; raise up to ~$100B on a ~$965B last private mark.

BASE RATE. SEC rules require public filing ≥15 days before the roadshow. Recent large-tech public-S-1-to-pricing intervals: Arm 23d, Instacart 24d, CoreWeave 24d, Figma 29d, Rivian 39d — median ~3.5 weeks, hard floor ~3 weeks. A late-September flip therefore prices ~Oct 21–28, not before Oct 17. Pricing by Oct 16 would need the flip within the next week AND a compressed roadshow, contradicting reporting that moved the date later, not earlier. Timelines that slip once rarely un-slip.

CROSS-VENUE CHECK. Polymarket (trading-open resolution, a strictly later event) has Oct 15 at 5% and Oct 31 at 57%. Mapping Kalshi's pricing trigger onto that curve gives roughly 8–13% for 'before Oct 17'. Kalshi's whole near-dated curve (Oct 10 at 8%, Oct 17 at 28%) is fat versus Polymarket's.

CROWD NARRATIVE. Retail reads 'Anthropic IPO in October' plus 'largest IPO ever' headlines and buys the mid-October strike without modeling the 15-day rule or roadshow length; the Oct 1 shutdown risk that could have stalled SEC effectiveness was also averted by a CR funding through December, so no NO-tailwind is being mispriced in my favor.

OTHER SIDE. YES buyers believe Anthropic sprints to beat a crowded AI-IPO window and election volatility. That is the real risk.

FALSIFIER. A public S-1 hitting EDGAR before ~Sep 18 with a launched roadshow by Oct 5 — or any exchange formally assigning the ticker — would break my thesis. If no public S-1 exists by Sep 25, NO is near-certain.
